role: the delivery manager who has seen hundred-task plans
verdict: No: the spec cannot land v1 as written, because its release path is forbidden by its own workflow grammar and has an unspecified signing step, the built product first meets real sbx after 91 tasks with every fix restarting a two-host block B, and most deferral triggers have no watcher once spec review rounds stop.

findings.defect: The workflow grammar allows only 'read' or 'none' permissions, no github.token, no secrets and no step env, yet release.yml must publish a release, attach dora.json, mint attestations and run gh, and 10 10.2 says the file passes tools/ci workflows.
findings.scenario: T088 writes release.yml with permissions contents: write, id-token: write and attestations: write and a GH_TOKEN for tools/release publish; tools/ci workflows fails it. Written within the grammar, the rc tag run fails at the attestation or publish step, and the tag ruleset leaves no clean retry under the same name. S1 cannot be met.
findings.change: Add to 10 10.2 one named exception for .github/workflows/release.yml only: a release job may hold contents: write, id-token: write and attestations: write, and the run steps of tools/release publish, tools/release verify and tools/ci dora --attach may receive GH_TOKEN from github.token through a step env key. The exception list lives in tools/ci beside the grammar, tools/ci workflows fails any other file that uses it, and a threat note says what the token can do inside that job. ci.yml stays read-only.
findings.cost: one grammar row, a fixture test per allowed key, a threat paragraph, an approval on the checks and dependencies surfaces

findings.defect: 'Release signing' fixes that signing is an operator step with a credential outside GitHub, but no tool, artifact, format, journey step, operator block or S1 evidence item exists, and S1 calls the keyless attestation the signature.
findings.scenario: At the v1.0.0 tag the maintainer finds no defined signing step: either v1.0.0 ships with checksums and attestations only, against 05 5.4, or a signing tool and key custody are chosen on the last stretch of the critical path and the release waits.
findings.change: Decide now, in 05 5.4 and S1, one of two texts. (a) v1 has no separate signature: the trust root is checksums.txt plus the build provenance attestation, and 'Release signing' becomes a deferred row with an observable trigger. (b) Name the tool and key custody, what is signed (checksums.txt), where the signature is published, the J1 verification step, an S1 evidence item, and an operator step in 10 10.2 'Release and bootstrap'.
findings.cost: a maintainer decision; for (b) a tool choice, a J1 step and an operator block

findings.defect: The build order brings the product to real sbx only at the release candidate (block B), while 10 10.3 lists VM boot, virtiofs, network policy, credential injection, kit builds and host-command prompts as things the fake cannot model.
findings.scenario: 91 tasks pass against the fake. The first real run finds that a mount, a policy argv or a kit build behaves differently. Each fix touches a path outside docs/, so 11 11.2 requires a new candidate and block B again, about 90 minutes per host on two Macs, for each iteration.
findings.change: Add to 12 12.2 two real-host smoke steps that are not block B results: after the sync slice (romeu init, sync, approve against real sbx on one host) and after run (J1 to J3 on one host, from a dry-run build of main). Each is one host-suite command whose result is pasted under Evidence and is not committed under docs/probes/. Replace the 'Residual rework risk' sentence, which asserts what these runs would test.
findings.cost: two short operator sittings in the build order, plus a selector in the host suite

findings.defect: Four completeness checks (the I-row tags of S6, every 'Settled by' probe result, a guide page per journey, the block B commit rule) run once, after the v1.0.0 release, 'because checking them on each PR would keep all red', and no rule says what happens when they fail after the tag.
findings.scenario: An invariant row whose test was never tagged, or a probe nobody ran (11 11.4: 'noticed only there'), surfaces in T102 after v1.0.0 is public. The release no longer meets S6 or S10, and the spec defines neither a yank nor a v1.0.1 path.
findings.change: Add a pending-ids file under tools/ci (on the checks surface) listing the I rows, probe ids and journeys not yet done. 'all' fails on any id that is done but still listed, or that is missing yet not listed; the file must be empty for a v* tag without a suffix and for the rc's pre-tag check. Keep acceptance as the final re-check. Add one sentence on a post-tag failure: a v1.0.1 carrying the fix with a Fixes-release trailer, decided by the maintainer.
findings.cost: one data file, one check, two sentences; the same edit retires the 11 11.4 reminder

findings.defect: Several triggers are not observable events (ADR 0005 rule 3), and no row names what detects its event, although ADR 0005 Consequences asks for it.
findings.scenario: Rows reopened by 'the operator saying so', 'the first question about the cost of one change', 'the first question about the ledger that query cannot answer', 'the first rejection that cannot be diagnosed', 'a consumer needs one', 'The maintainer observes these', 'a lesson has to be learned again on a second machine' and 'the first dark package found more than one release after it merged' never fire, because no tool or person is assigned to notice them. tools/ci sequences passes them because all three cells are filled.
findings.change: Add a fourth column, 'Detected by', naming a check, a command output or the issue label that records the event, and have tools/ci sequences require it. Rewrite each listed row to an event that has a detector (an issue with a label, a doctor warning, a diff to a named file), or move it to a list of ideas with no promise.

postmortem: After v1.0.0 the product shipped late and the maintainer stopped dogfooding it. (1) The first real run came last: 91 tasks ran against a fake that cannot model VM boot, virtiofs, policy, credential injection or kit builds; the rehearsal found architecture-level problems, and each fix needed a new candidate and block B on two Macs (12 12.2, 10 10.3, 11 11.2, 10 10.5). (2) The release workflow could not exist under the grammar's read-only permissions and no-token rule, and signing, 'an operator step', had no tool; v1.0.0 shipped with attestations only and S1 was argued after the fact (10 10.2, 05 5.4, S1, ADR 0008). (3) The operator was the queue: most PRs needed approval words, every merge waited, blocks A and B needed both Macs, and gate 1 asked for a TTY on each dev build; the wait metric could not tell who merged and arrived in phase 8 (05 5.3, 12 12.4, 12 12.10, 11 11.1, 01 1.4). (4) The kits stood on a milestone frontend with no plan B and no re-probe rule; recordings went stale with an sbx upgrade (06 6.1, Q7, 10 10.3, 11 11.4). (5) Success was checked after shipping: tag, probe and guide completeness ran once, after the tag (index Success criteria, 10 10.5, 05 5.2, 11 11.4). (6) The ledger took a phase with no criterion needing it and no cut line (13, 00 0.5, ADR 0006). (7) Deferrals never fired: the table was read in review rounds that ended; the token trigger fired at the rc and changed the sandbox during block B (index Deferred decisions, ADR 0005, ADR 0008, 05 5.4). (8) The records misled: ADR 0002 and 0003 still claimed a review and a person who merges; dora reported empty metrics for the whole build, and change fail rate later read zero for want of trailers (ADR 0002, ADR 0003, ADR 0004, 12 12.9, 12 12.10). (9) Unsaid: a team-sized process run by one person and agents spent the one scarce resource, the maintainer's sittings, and no budget for it was written anywhere (05 5.3, 10 10.2, ADR 0001, 12 12.4).
lens_critique: This lens measures success as the plan landing on time with an operator who never idles, but in this product the operator's sittings are the security control itself: TTY gates, untruncated diffs and ask-first words exist so that a person reads. Optimising operator idle time pushes toward batching and shortcuts that weaken the boundary the product sells. And with one maintainer and no deadline, the real failure is not a late v1 but a correct v1 that is abandoned because it costs too much to run; schedule and DORA throughput matter less here than the sustainability of the operator's effort, which this lens only partly sees.
missing_viewpoint: The sponsor who pays: nobody in L0 to L16 owns cost and sustainability as one budget (agent compute and tokens, Actions quota, the maintainer's hours per release, and whether one person can keep this running a year after v1); L14 and L3 touch maintenance, not the economics that decide whether it survives.
